name: Laminated with UV-filtering PVB
process: As 'laminated', with a PVB that carries more UV absorber, so the laminate passes almost nothing below 400 nm, the conventional boundary of light. This is how the daylit galleries meet their UV limit without blinds: the glazing itself is the filter (D-014).

uvBoundary.note: 'Convention assigns the boundary between UV and light at 400 nm, but slight perception begins at 380 nm.'

uvBehindLaminateBound.derivation: an upper bound: daylight UV (at most 1000 uW/lm, CCI) times the laminate's transmitted UV (under 0.01 from 300 to 400 nm, Saflex UV) over its visible transmittance (0.88). Art.WithinCare measures the real value with Light's probe.
uvBehindLaminateBound.source: S. Michalski, 'Agent of Deterioration: Light, Ultraviolet and Infrared', Canadian Conservation Institute, 2018-05-17, https://www.canada.ca/en/conservation-institute/services/agents-deterioration/light.html ; Eastman, 'Product technical data: Saflex UV polyvinyl butyral interlayer (RB4U)', Applications Technical Documentation 031720 (UV screening 99 % up to 400 nm; optical and solar data for 3 mm clear / 0.76 mm / 3 mm clear), https://saflex-vanceva.eastman.com/content/dam/saflex/pdf-documents/arch/saflex-uv/Product%20Technical%20Sheet%20-%20Saflex%20UV.pdf

yellowing.text: Filtration around 380-400 nm causes slight yellowing of the light due to the reduction of violet radiation at the edge of the visible range.
yellowing.source: J. Tetreault, C. Anuzet, 'Ultraviolet Filters', CCI Notes 2/1, Canadian Conservation Institute, 2015, https://www.canada.ca/en/conservation-institute/services/conservation-preservation-publications/canadian-conservation-institute-notes/ultraviolet-filters.html

fadingEvidence.text: In 148 days of outdoor exposure over the summer of 2021 (5 May to 6 November) behind laminates of two 4 mm panes, the 400 nm interlayer (Trosifol Extra Protect) measurably delayed the fading of medium-stable samples (Blue Wool 4 to 7, most clearly 5 and 6) compared with the 380 nm standard PVB (Trosifol Ultra Clear); the benefit depends on the colourant and exposure time and was not reduced to one number.
fadingEvidence.source: M. Mueller, S. Reich, C. Pfuetze, I. Stelzer, 'Investigation of color protection of laminated glass by UV-blocking interlayers for conservation application', Glass Structures & Engineering (2024), doi:10.1007/s40940-023-00246-9; summary at https://www.glassonweb.com/article/investigation-color-protection-laminated-glass-uv-blocking-interlayers-conservation

laminatedGlassScreensUva.text: Clear glass screens nearly all UVB but little UVA; laminated glass with UV-absorbing interlayers screens both.
laminatedGlassScreensUva.source: National Glass Association, Glass Technical Paper FB34-12 (2023) 'Screening Out Ultraviolet Radiation with Laminated Glass', https://www.glass.org/sites/default/files/2023-04/FB34-12_2023_Screening_Out_Ultraviolet_Radiation_with_Laminated_Glass.pdf

photograph: The light behind it is a touch warmer: the violet edge of the spectrum is cut.
